name: Weight Plate Pinch Press
description: The weight plate pinch press is a unique chest exercise in which two weight plates are pressed together between the palms and pushed overhead or forward. The act of pinching the plates isometrically activates the pectoral muscles throughout the pressing motion, making it an excellent finishing or isolation movement for inner chest development.

execution.starting_position: Hold two smooth-faced weight plates sandwich-style between your palms at chest level. Stand or lie on a flat bench.
execution.setup_instructions: Choose two plates of equal size (10lb plates are common). Smooth faces should be in contact with each other. Grip the outer edges with palms facing inward.
steps: Step 1: Squeeze the plates firmly together and hold them at chest level.
Step 2: Keeping the squeeze constant, press the plates forward (standing) or upward (lying) until the arms are extended.
Step 3: Hold the top position and intensify the squeeze for 1 second.
Step 4: Lower the plates back to the starting position while continuing to press inward.
Step 5: Never release the squeeze between reps.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale as you press the plates away. Inhale as you bring them back to the chest.
common_mistakes: Releasing the inward squeeze on the press, allowing plates to slide
Using plates with rough or ridged outer faces that cut into the palms
Going too heavy and losing control of the pinch
safety_considerations: Use smooth-faced steel plates, not bumper plates with raised lips
Do not use this exercise to failure — dropping the plates could cause injury
Start with lighter plates until the pinch coordination feels stable
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Press to full arm extension, maintaining the inward squeeze the entire time. Lower under control.
coaching_cues: Squeeze the plates like your life depends on it
Feel the sternum compress on the press
Don't let the squeeze go — that IS the exercise
